Tengfei Long is an associate research professor and master's supervisor at the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). He was selected for the CAS Youth Innovation Promotion Association and a CAS distinguished research appointment (backbone position). He serves as a Topic Editor for Remote Sensing and a member of the early-career editorial board of Remote Sensing Technology and Application. His research focuses on intelligent remote-sensing information processing and applications, including high-accuracy image registration, large-scale forest and burned area mapping, and remote sensing for human well-being, such as economic well-being, thermal environments, and public health. He developed the world's first global 30 m burned area product (GABAM), offering an order-of-magnitude improvement in spatial resolution over comparable international products. He has published more than 100 papers, including over 40 SCI-indexed papers as first or corresponding author, received 16 invention patents, and contributed to six monographs and one national standard. His honors include science and technology progress awards from Beijing and Hainan, the Geoinformation Science and Technology Progress Award, the Surveying and Mapping Science and Technology Award, and the China Lighting Award.
